decisions.reason: As a classic door lever handle line, it sits squarely in the firm's core mechanical hardware knowledge base, so the firm is well placed to refine and commercialize it rather than withdraw it.

This door lever handle family closely matches the firm's established design, engineering and certification capabilities, making continued learning and portfolio support more likely than discontinuation.
Although a single door handle design is somewhat easier to prune than a broader system line, it still builds on highly related competencies in architectural fittings and design-led differentiation.
This product is strongly related to the firm's existing know-how, but as another handle design in a broad portfolio it faces a slightly higher rationalization risk if overlap appears.
A handle family fits the firm's accumulated knowledge in materials, fixing technology, ergonomics and compliance, so management would likely keep it and learn from early market response.

The electronic access system is a strategic flagship aligned with the firm's move toward digital building organization and supported by its innovation, system and access-control capabilities, so withdrawal is unlikely.
